messages:
anya: Heads up — seeing intermittent missing traces from eval-runner in prod for the quantization experiments. A few completed jobs show 0 artifacts in S3 even though runner logs say 'upload succeeded'.

julian: ugh. can you paste a log snippet? is this limited to large batches or a particular model/version?

anya: pasted below. looks like the runner writes a temp file then POSTs to the storage service. sometimes the upload call returns 200 but the manifest doesn't include the sample keys. only on high-concurrency jobs (~200 concurrent shards).

anya: ```
[2026-02-12T14:02:11Z] INFO shard=17 wrote /tmp/eval-17-1745.ndjson.gz
[2026-02-12T14:02:11Z] INFO shard=17 upload /tmp/eval-17-1745.ndjson.gz -> s3://eval-artifacts/2026/02/12/eval-1745/part-17.gz status=200
[2026-02-12T14:02:11Z] WARN shard=17 manifest-upload returned 409 existing keys mismatch
```

sasha: 409 on manifest upload implies a race when multiple shards are trying to write the same manifest object key. we used a naive `manifest.json` PUT that overwrites.

miguel: yep — runner does: 1) upload part file 2) read manifest.json 3) append key 4) PUT manifest.json. concurrent ops race and one PUT clobbers the other, leaving some parts unlisted but files still present in bucket. dashboards only look at manifest so shows 0 artifacts.

anya: that explains it. seen this fail on the new quantized LLM runs because we increased shards. any quick mitigations?

julian: short term: make manifest writes idempotent by switching to S3 `PutObject` with `x-amz-server-side-encryption` and using deterministic keys per part (uuid) then use an atomic manifest update via S3 Object Lock? too heavy. Better: write a per-shard manifest (part-17.meta) and then have a manifest-aggregator job that lists prefix and composes final manifest via server-side list.

sasha: +1 for per-shard manifests. or use S3 multipart upload for the final manifest with `UploadPartCopy` — but that is more work. per-shard meta means the aggregator can be retried safely.

miguel: also we should avoid a single manifest object as the canonical source. Dashboards should count files via listing and reconcile with manifest for speed. Listing is slower but accurate. Add a periodic reconciler to surface discrepancies.

anya: two related asks: 1) storage cost ballooning because some shards uploaded duplicate files during retries (we don't dedupe by content hash), 2) preserve full per-sample metadata schema (we lost tokenizer_version in some old runs).

julian: for cost: compute SHA256 per shard and use that as filename prefix: `sha256-<hex>.ndjson.gz`. If a retry uploads same content, we can skip storing duplicate by checking `HeadObject` first. For metadata schema: let's standardize on NDJSON with fields: `sample_id, eval_id, model_version, tokenizer_version, prompt_template, seed, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, quality_score, tags`. And compress with gzip.

sasha: agree. throw a small header in each file with `schema_version` to make future migrations easier. Example NDJSON line: `{"sample_id":"s-123","eval_id":"e-456","model":"gptq-v2","tokenizer_v":"v1.3","latency_ms":234,"quality_score":0.84,"output":"..."}`

miguel: also need to be careful with PII in outputs — add a consent flag and a redaction pipeline that can run as a post-process step before files hit long-term storage. For now mark these runs as `redaction_required=true` so aggregator pauses finalization until redaction completes.

ci-bot: Reminder: last PR that touched eval-runner storage client failed the integration smoke test 2/3 times on circleci due to flaky S3 mocking.

julian: we should add a small end-to-end test in CI that spins up 4 parallel shards and verifies final manifest contains all parts. That would have caught this.

anya: I'm going to open a small PR that: - write per-shard meta objects - change filenames to include sha256 - add `schema_version: "v2"` in each file - add aggregator job to compose final manifest idempotently

sasha: please also add a migration script to reconcile existing buckets: list objects for the eval prefix, compute manifest from listed parts, and update dashboards. We'll need to mark reconciled runs with `reconciled: true` in metadata.

miguel: retention policy: recommend keeping full NDJSON artifacts for 90 days hot, then move to Glacier/Cold after 30 days if `cost_sensitive=true` workflows. But regulatory customers may need longer retention — make retention configurable per-tenant. Also add a `trace_sample_rate` field per eval.

anya: proposal for sampling: default `trace_sample_rate=0.01` for regular runs, and `trace_sample_rate=1.0` for regression/eval-debug runs (run flagged with `full_trace=true`). For expensive quantization sweeps we probably want 0.001 to reduce costs. Document this in eval templates.

julian: also add `trace_summary` quick metrics uploaded to metrics DB (count, avg latency, p95, num_errors) so dashboard shows health even when we only sample traces.

sasha: implementation details for aggregator: 1) list `s3://eval-artifacts/<eval-id>/` 2) read all `*.meta` files 3) dedupe by `sha256` 4) write `manifest.json` with a `parts` array and `schema_version` 5) write `manifest.complete` marker object with a `created_by` field and `etag` 6) dashboards watch for `manifest.complete` to switch run to "available". This avoids 409 races.

miguel: and make the aggregator idempotent and run it as a short-lived lambda or k8s job with a backoff. If aggregator sees `manifest.complete` it verifies counts and optionally reissues manifest if mismatch.

anya: I'll add a simple repro job that runs with `--concurrency 250` locally to try to reproduce flakiness reliably. If we can reproduce we can test the per-shard meta approach quickly.

julian: sounds good. Can you also add a smoke CI job that runs with concurrency 8 in PRs touching the storage client? That should catch basic races.

anya: yes. I'll draft the PR today and link here. cc @julian for review.

ops-bot: Scheduled: eval-artifact-reconciler job will run nightly at 03:00 UTC to surface missing manifests.

sasha: Thanks — once PR is up I'll help with the migration script and update the dashboards to use listing fallback. :thumbsup:

anya: PR: https://stash.redwood.internal/p/redwood/eval-runner/pull/412

julian: look for my review tomorrow morning. If we need an emergency hotfix, we can gate new quantization runs until reconciler finishes.

anya: noted. thanks all.
